To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of 13-phenethyl and 13-dibenzhydryl berberines to human telomeric G-quartets is stronger than berberine and that this interaction is responsible for their cytotoxic effect on cancer cells.

(i) 13-substituted berberine analogues (NAX) bind to human telomeric G-quartets with different affinities, (ii) the crystal structure of NAX053-Tet12 adduct shows that the ligand interacts via π-staking, sandwiched at interface of two symmetry related quadruplex unit, (iii) NAX042 and 053 are the most effective ligands in improving the performance of berberine.
the 13-phenylethyl berberine derivative NAX042 is a good ligand for human telomeric G-quartets.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, synthesis, and biological evaluation of a series of berberine derivatives, with the aim of developing new anticancer agents.
the development of a novel class of berberine derivatives as potential anticancer agents.
the identification of a new class of berberine derivatives that can be used as potential G4 ligands for the treatment of human cancers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
13-phenylethyl and 13-benzyl berberine are able to bind human telomeric G4 structures, and the 13-benzhydryl substituent is able to improve the interaction.
the 13-alkyl-13-arylberberine derivatives are promising G4 ligands and, at the same time, cytotoxic agents. 13-Phenylalkyl and Diphenylalkyl Berberine
NAX042 and 053 are promising candidates for further development as telomerase inhibitors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 13-substituted berberine derivatives, NAX, are able to bind to the human telomeric G4 structure and to inhibit its formation.

the introduction of a phenylalkyl substituent at the C13 position of berberine, in combination with a second phenylalkyl group, is a successful strategy to improve the interaction with the human telomeric G4 structure, and consequently to increase its antiproliferative activity.
13-dipenylalkyl berbines have the best affinity for G4 and the best cytotoxic effect on cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the introduction of a phenylalkyl or diphenylalkyl group at the 13-position of the berberine scaffold is a promising approach to improve its anticancer activity and to develop new G4 ligands with a better therapeutic index.
the binding of the 13-substituted berberines to the G4 structure is a promising strategy to improve the anticancer efficacy of these natural compounds.

the binding of NAX compounds to the human telomeric quadruplexes can be modulated by the length of the linker and by the presence of the benzhydryl moiety, which can be considered as a promising scaffold for the design of novel telomerase inhibitors.
